title: Ensuring Continuous Operation in MRT Network Even with Service Disruptions along Some Parts
what_it_is: Ensuring Continuous Operation in MRT Network Even with Service Disruptions along Some Parts

sections.label: MRT disruption contingency measures
sections.summary: Operators may run bi-directional or loop services, use buses, and rely on condition monitoring and pump systems; the oldest lines will be fully renewed by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: For example, if a section of one track is down, the operator may run bi-directional services on the unaffected track.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: If train services are disrupted on a section of both tracks, the operator may turn trains around to run loop services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Buses may also be used to ferry commuters across stations with no service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We do not rely primarily on train drivers to detect abnormalities along the tracks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Condition monitoring equipment is deployed to monitor the status of key systems, such as trackside power and signalling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Pump systems are installed in underground tunnels and stations to drain away water from tunnel washing and seepages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The North-South and East-West Lines are our oldest MRT lines and they have started to exhibit age-reliability issues, such as wear-and-tear and equipment obsolescence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The lines will be fully renewed by 2024.
